pl-l2d25c7-d1e108.summary: States that besides other penalties man incurred the corruption and depression of free choice: natural goods were corrupted and gratuitous goods withdrawn. He is the man wounded and stripped by robbers, wounded in natural goods, not deprived of them or restoration were impossible, and stripped of gratuitous goods added by grace. Natural goods like talent, memory, and intellect were corrupted, gratuitous ones removed, though natural goods too belong to God's general grace. So freedom of choice was corrupted and partly lost.
claims: Sin wounded natural goods and removed gratuitous goods.
Free choice was corrupted and partly lost.

pl-l2d25c7-d1e113.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: misusing free choice, man lost himself and it; conquered by sin, he lost free choice, being enslaved to his conqueror. Augustine means not that man has no free choice after sin, but that he lost its freedom, not all, but freedom from misery and from sin.
claims: Man lost freedom from sin and misery, not free choice itself.

pl-l2d25c7.summary: Concludes that besides other penalties, man incurred corruption and depression of free choice: natural goods were corrupted and gratuitous goods withdrawn. He is the man wounded and stripped by robbers (Luke 10:30): wounded in natural goods (talent, memory, intellect), not deprived of them or he could not be restored, and stripped of gratuitous goods added by grace, though natural goods too belong to God's general grace. So freedom of choice was corrupted and partly lost. Augustine: misusing free choice, man lost himself and it; not that he lacked free choice after sin, but he lost freedom from misery and sin.
claims: Natural goods were wounded, gratuitous goods withdrawn.
The man wounded and stripped by robbers figures fallen humanity.
Natural goods were not removed, or restoration would be impossible.
Man lost freedom from sin and misery, not free choice itself.
